target_customer: Engineering, manufacturing and quality teams, including aerospace and defense, that review drawings
problem: GD&T callouts are interpreted inconsistently, so errors surface late in stack-ups, manufacturing or the field.
business_model: Software licences (F4 Review, Pro, Enterprise tiers); prices not listed

founders.name: Paul Shin
founders.background_notes: YC page also cites liquid bipropellant rocketry work at 'UA & UC Berkeley'

founders.name: Aidan Cantu
education: B.S. and M.S. Electrical Engineering, minors in CS and Math (YC page; school not named)

technical_complexity.rationale: Encoding ASME Y14.5 rules deterministically and computing stack-ups from drawings and 3D files runs on-device without AI.

defensibility.rationale: A rules engine across several Y14.5 editions is slow to build, but AI drawing review tools such as CoLab address the same pain.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent response found; a 2026 comparison says CAD tools provide tolerance features but not drawing checkers.

market_need_then: Founders cite late-found GD&T errors as costly; comparison pages show demand for drawing checking tools, though dated early evidence was not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and confident, e.g. 'See GD&T Issues Instantly'

brand_strength.rationale: Alphanumeric name shared with many unrelated products (F4 is also used by other companies), no brand press found.

outcome_analysis: F4 is an active YC Summer 2025 company with two founders from Tesla and SpaceX selling a deterministic GD&T analysis platform. No funding round, customer or outcome is documented beyond aggregator figures. Its no-AI positioning is a distinct angle versus AI drawing review tools, but adoption and sales traction are unknown.
notes: Unverified funding: aggregators list 500K pre-seed (Sept 2025) with Y Combinator and 468 Capital; no primary source. Competitor search returned 2026 listicles only; list empty. Name origin not found.
